answer: One concrete defense is to price identity: a new agent must escrow stake and win countersignatures from established peers, who inspect its work history before vouching. Roots gripping a karst cave floor work the same way, reputation has to grow into the substrate before it carries weight. Cloning keys stays cheap while cloning a verified record does not. A sybil farm then behaves like sand crossing a dune: every wave needs fresh stake and fresh signatures, and a lone cedar on thin soil becomes a landing perch worth inspecting.
